subject: Lavaan - CFA - categorical variables - the last threshold is strange

messages.author: 0df59cf628558349
messages.subject: Lavaan - CFA - categorical variables - the last threshold is strange
parts:
I have a problem to perform a multiple group CFA with Lavaan (R).

Indeed, I have several categorical variables and some variables contains 11 categories. So I will have 10 thresholds for these variables. In attached you can found a part of my results. In this picture you can see that I have 10 thresholds but the 10th thresholds is smaller than the 9th, it is not in the creasing order. I have several variables with 11 categories and it is the same problem for each of these variables.

My question is : Why is not in the creasing order?


Here, you can find a part of my R-code:

(At this point it is just my model without the group option but after I perform the same thing with the group option and I have the same problem for the thresholds)

model2<-'range = ~ NA*gvjbevn + gvhlthc + gvslvol + gvslvue + gvcldcr + gvpdlwk

goals = ~ NA*sbprvpv + sbeqsoc + sbcwkfm

range~~1*range

goals~~1*goals

gvhlthc ~~ gvslvol

gvcldcr ~~ gvpdlwk

'

cfa.model2<-cfa(model2, ordered=varcat, estimator="WLSMV",data=sub)

summary(cfa.model2,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE, modindices=TRUE)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Lavaan - CFA - categorical variables - the last threshold is strange
parts: Indeed, I have several categorical variables and some variables contains 11 categories.

Thresholds are labeled "t1, t2, ...t[nCategories - 1]", which are character strings.  Thus, they are assigned by default (in R) in alphabetical order (i.e., t10 comes alphabetically between t1 and t2, and you can see that the t10 threshold is indeed between the t1 and t2 thresholds).  I'm sure that is just a situation the developer didn't plan for because I doubt many researchers would hesitate to treat an 11-category ordinal variable as continuous.  Rhemtulla et al. showed that you can treat even 7-category ordinal variables as continuous indicators without noticeably attenuated estimates or biased test statistics using robust MLE:

http://psych.colorado.edu/~willcutt/pdfs/Rhemtulla_2012.pdf
